title: Coapt pattern-recognition myoelectric prostheses attached to transulnar osseointegration implants restore daily-living control in two patients
summary: Two transulnar amputees given Coapt pattern-recognition prostheses on osseointegration implants regained activities of daily living.
account: A JBJS Case Connector report published 15 December 2021 (Jaime, Reif, Kafedzic, Garrison, Dhawan and Rozbruch) describes two people with traumatic transulnar amputations who underwent osseointegration implantation. After surgery a myoelectric prosthesis fitted with Coapt pattern-recognition software, which classifies electromyographic signal patterns to drive a multiarticulating hand and wrist, was attached directly to the implant, and both patients trained with the software. At the most recent follow-ups of 18 months and 2 years the implants showed no loosening, and the authors state that prosthetic control gradually improved to allow activities of daily living. Surgery dates are not given in the read abstract, so the publication date is used.
purpose: Pattern-recognition control of a multiarticulating myoelectric hand and wrist for people with upper-limb amputation
system: Coapt pattern recognition myoelectric control (Coapt, Chicago, IL) on a multiarticulating hand and wrist
deployer: Hospital for Special Surgery, New York (Department of Limb Lengthening and Complex Reconstruction; the affiliation is given for the first author)
location: New York, New York, United States

ratings.reason: Two identifiable patients gained prosthetic control sufficient for activities of daily living, documented at 18-month and 2-year follow-up; the abstract gives no validated functional scores, so -3 is not supported.
A two-patient case report demonstrating feasibility of combining osseointegration with pattern-recognition control; no population-level effect shown.

ai_role.statement: The Coapt software is a machine-learning pattern-recognition controller that maps electromyographic patterns to hand and wrist motions; the report attributes improved control to training with this software on an osseointegrated attachment, so the AI contribution is entangled with the surgical attachment and cannot be isolated.

evidence.citation: Jaime KM, Reif TJ, Kafedzic H, Garrison G, Dhawan J, Rozbruch SR (2021). Attachment of a Myoelectric Prosthesis After Transulnar Osseointegration Implantation: A 2-Patient Case Study. JBJS Case Connector 11(4).
evidence.title: Attachment of a Myoelectric Prosthesis After Transulnar Osseointegration Implantation: A 2-Patient Case Study
evidence.quote: After surgery, a myoelectric prosthetic equipped with Coapt (Chicago, IL) recognition software was attached directly to the implant.

evidence.citation: Simon AM, Turner KL, Miller LA, Potter BK, Beachler MD, Dumanian GA, Hargrove LJ, Kuiken TA (2023). User Performance With a Transradial Multi-Articulating Hand Prosthesis During Pattern Recognition and Direct Control Home Use. IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng.
evidence.title: User Performance With a Transradial Multi-Articulating Hand Prosthesis During Pattern Recognition and Direct Control Home Use
evidence.quote: they showed significant improvements in the Assessment of Capacity for Myoelectric Control (ACMC) outcome measure while using pattern recognition control compared to direct control

produced_by: Stable implanted attachment delivering consistent electrode contact
Pattern-recognition classifier trained on the patient's own EMG patterns
Structured training with the software after surgery
must_hold: Sufficient residual muscle signals to separate grip and wrist classes
Osseointegration without loosening over the follow-up period

echoes.setting: Randomized 8-week home trials of pattern recognition versus direct control with the Coapt system in transradial amputees (cohort)
echoes.model_version: Coapt COMPLETE CONTROL with Ossur i-Limb Ultra Revolution
echoes.source: Simon et al. (2023) IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng, PMID 36355739

headline: Coapt pattern recognition restores daily living for two amputees

comparator.after: significant improvements in the Assessment of Capacity for Myoelectric Control (ACMC) outcome measure while using pattern recognition control compared to direct control
comparator.quote: After the home trial, they showed significant improvements in the Assessment of Capacity for Myoelectric Control (ACMC) outcome measure while using pattern recognition control compared to direct control; other outcome measures showed no differences between control styles.

later.note: A later randomized home-use study of transradial amputees confirmed broader grip use and better myoelectric control with Coapt pattern recognition than with direct control.
later.quote: While at home, participants demonstrated broader usage of grips in pattern recognition compared to direct control.
